A **FHIR Implementation Guide** is a published, versioned package of profiles,
terminology, examples and prose that says how FHIR is to be used for one
purpose. In this knowledge graph it is content of a particular shape, and the
shape is what this page is about.

Two things distinguish it from the other content kinds here. It is
**compiled** — an author writes FHIR Shorthand and a tool produces the
resources, so the thing an author edits and the thing a reader fetches are
different artefacts. And it is **published at canonical URLs** that other IGs
resolve against, so its identity is a URL and a version rather than a path in
a repository.

Both have consequences that catch people out, and each is a section below.

## L1, L2, L3 — three layers, not three stages
{: #the-three-layers data-fa-label="sec:fhir-content-the-three-layers" }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/folio-assistant/edit/main/content/docs/fhir-content/the-three-layers.md){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit content/docs/fhir-content/the-three-layers.md" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><span class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-unswept fa-qa-fam-block" title="Content QA: not swept — no sidecar for this block" aria-label="Content QA: not swept — no sidecar for this block"><span class="fa-qa-tag">QA</span></span> <span class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-unswept fa-qa-fam-translation" title="Translation QA: not swept — no sidecar for this block" aria-label="Translation QA: not swept — no sidecar for this block"><span class="fa-qa-tag">TR</span></span></span>

WHO SMART Guidelines names three layers, and they are the clearest available
vocabulary for FHIR content generally:

| layer | what it holds | form |
|---|---|---|
| **L1** | narrative guidance — the publication a recommendation comes from | prose, figures, tables |
| **L2** | the Digital Adaptation Kit — personas, business processes, decision logic, data elements | BPMN, DMN, structured tables |
| **L3** | the FHIR Implementation Guide | FSH → FHIR resources |

**They are layers, not stages, and the difference is load-bearing.** A stage
model says each is produced from the one before and then left behind. In
practice all three are live at once: an L2 decision table and the L3
`PlanDefinition` derived from it both exist, both are published, and both can
change. Treating L2 as scaffolding that L3 replaces is how a decision table
and its FHIR representation drift apart with nothing to notice.

It is also why an instance may hold any one of the three without the others.
An L1 corpus with no DAK behind it is a real thing; so is an IG with no L1.

## Representations, and why only one is taken
{: #representations data-fa-label="sec:fhir-content-representations" }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/folio-assistant/edit/main/content/docs/fhir-content/representations.md){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit content/docs/fhir-content/representations.md" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><span class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-unswept fa-qa-fam-block" title="Content QA: not swept — no sidecar for this block" aria-label="Content QA: not swept — no sidecar for this block"><span class="fa-qa-tag">QA</span></span> <span class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-unswept fa-qa-fam-translation" title="Translation QA: not swept — no sidecar for this block" aria-label="Translation QA: not swept — no sidecar for this block"><span class="fa-qa-tag">TR</span></span></span>

The IG Publisher emits **three serialisations of every resource** — JSON, XML
and Turtle — plus HTML per resource page.

This platform's render path takes the **JSON**, wrapped in JSON-LD and JSON
Schema. That is a decision rather than an omission: three serialisations of
one resource are three chances to disagree about what the resource says, and
the JSON-LD wrapper carries the semantics the other two were being kept for.
An instance that genuinely needs RDF gets it by projecting the JSON-LD, not by
shipping the Publisher's Turtle.

**A representation that arrives and is not taken is recorded as a refusal.**
Otherwise "this IG publishes no Turtle" and "we ignored its Turtle" become the
same observation, and only one of them is a fact about the IG.

The `.html` case is different and worth separating. The Publisher's HTML is
not a serialisation of a resource — it is a *rendering*, with the Publisher's
own navigation, theme and cross-links baked in. Mounting it is what this
platform is moving away from, because finished HTML carries no front matter:
the navbar, the language bar, the QA badges and the translation surface all
stop at its edge.

## The artefact index is reconstructed
{: #the-artefact-index data-fa-label="sec:fhir-content-the-artefact-index" }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/folio-assistant/edit/main/content/docs/fhir-content/the-artefact-index.md){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit content/docs/fhir-content/the-artefact-index.md" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><span class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-unswept fa-qa-fam-block" title="Content QA: not swept — no sidecar for this block" aria-label="Content QA: not swept — no sidecar for this block"><span class="fa-qa-tag">QA</span></span> <span class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-unswept fa-qa-fam-translation" title="Translation QA: not swept — no sidecar for this block" aria-label="Translation QA: not swept — no sidecar for this block"><span class="fa-qa-tag">TR</span></span></span>

**No FHIR IG publishes an index of its own artefacts.** This is the fact that
shapes every attempt to read one back as a graph, and it surprises people
because a published IG plainly *knows* what it contains.

What exists instead is four partial views, and none is sufficient alone:

| view | carries |
|---|---|
| `package.tgz` → `package/.index.json` | filename, `resourceType`, `id` for every file |
| `canonicals.json` | id, type, url, version, name — canonical resources only |
| `artifacts.html` | the only source of an artefact's **category** |
| `package.manifest.json` | package-level metadata |

So an index is **reconstructed**, and each field records which published file
it came from. The provenance is not bookkeeping: coverage differs per IG, and
badly. `canonicals.json` covers about a tenth of one WHO IG's artefacts and
all of another's. A pipeline that picked a winner on the first IG it met would
be silently wrong on the second, reporting a clean run over the artefacts that
view does not reach.

Two traps are documented because both have been hit:

- **`ValueSets.schema.json` at the published root is a schema, not an index.**
  It describes an enumeration endpoint's response and carries an `example`
  that holds the list — and the hub page links it to a `schemas/` directory it
  is not in.
- **`openapi/openapi.json` is not the DAK API.** In at least one WHO IG it is
  an unrelated domain API, so an ingest that globs for OpenAI-shaped files
  mis-files it.

## The DAK API surface
{: #the-dak-surface data-fa-label="sec:fhir-content-the-dak-surface" }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/folio-assistant/edit/main/content/docs/fhir-content/the-dak-surface.md){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit content/docs/fhir-content/the-dak-surface.md" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><span class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-unswept fa-qa-fam-block" title="Content QA: not swept — no sidecar for this block" aria-label="Content QA: not swept — no sidecar for this block"><span class="fa-qa-tag">QA</span></span> <span class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-unswept fa-qa-fam-translation" title="Translation QA: not swept — no sidecar for this block" aria-label="Translation QA: not swept — no sidecar for this block"><span class="fa-qa-tag">TR</span></span></span>

A WHO SMART Guidelines IG publishes an extra layer on top of standard IG
output — the **DAK API** — produced by scripts that run *after* the Publisher
exits:

- `<stem>.schema.json` — a JSON Schema per logical model and per ValueSet
- `<stem>.displays.json` — display labels
- `<stem>.openapi.json` — an OpenAPI description
- `<stem>.jsonld` — a JSON-LD vocabulary, built from ValueSet **expansions**
- `dak-api.html` — the hub a reader enters through

Its size varies by two orders of magnitude between IGs, so treat any figure
you have seen as a fact about one IG at one version rather than as a property
of the surface.

**None of this is the Publisher's work**, which is the practical reason to
know the boundary: a question about why a schema is missing is a question
about a post-processing script, not about the build. And because the JSON-LD
vocabularies are built from expansions, they inherit the terminology server's
availability — a thin vocabulary may mean a thin ValueSet or may mean nobody
could expand it, and the artefact alone does not say which.

## Where the rules live
{: #where-the-rules-live data-fa-label="sec:fhir-content-where-the-rules-live" }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/folio-assistant/edit/main/content/docs/fhir-content/where-the-rules-live.md){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit content/docs/fhir-content/where-the-rules-live.md" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><span class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-unswept fa-qa-fam-block" title="Content QA: not swept — no sidecar for this block" aria-label="Content QA: not swept — no sidecar for this block"><span class="fa-qa-tag">QA</span></span> <span class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-unswept fa-qa-fam-translation" title="Translation QA: not swept — no sidecar for this block" aria-label="Translation QA: not swept — no sidecar for this block"><span class="fa-qa-tag">TR</span></span></span>

This page describes the content. The rules are skills, and where the two
disagree the skill wins and this page is wrong:

- **`l2-dak-authoring`** and **`l3-fhir-authoring`** — authoring at each
  layer, and deriving rather than retyping.
- **`terminology-management`** — why terminology has its own lane, and the
  rule against inventing a code.
- **`fhir-validation`** — the two binaries, and why an absent capability did
  not pass.
- **`ig-artifact-ingestion`** — reading a published IG back as a graph: which
  IGs qualify, what to read, what to refuse.
- **`ig-render-jekyll`** — the three contracts for rendering IG content as
  folio pages, including the JSON-only rule above.
- **`smart-stack-layering`** — which harness layer a given asset belongs to,
  and the question that settles it.

For the tool that compiles and validates all of this, see
[The FHIR IG Publisher](ig-publisher.html).
